description: The frontend's Skill surface: what discovery may render about a skill, and what it must never become. A Skill is procedural knowledge (how) - not a capability (what) and not an agent (who). The catalog ships EMPTY on purpose: the contract is published and this consumer is a discovery surface, so it lists nothing it was not handed. What the UI renders with no declaration is the canonical unsupported answer, never a starter set of skills.

publication.note: The row this manifest was verified against, not a row this package may read. XA-19 was resolved by adopting the implemented P2.12 shape; register/select/load/release stay internal registry lifecycle methods. There is no execute operation and no ai:skill:execute permission at any layer.

rules: Discovery only: listing, search, filter, detail and selection validation read declarations. Nothing here selects, loads or executes a skill.
The six lifecycle states are six facts. No boolean `enabled` is derived from them, and none of them is an execution state.
A skill carries neither a permission nor an authority: the declared operation permissions are requirements of a backend operation, never a grant the UI holds.
The published operations are exactly four (skill.list, skill.resolve, skill.describe, skill.validate-selection). `load` is not one of them: discovering a skill never pulls its procedure.
With no declaration handed over, the canonical unsupported state is rendered: no fallback capability, no execution control and no tool list.
Skill entries are supplied to the runtime by the application; this package never reads the backend tree.

A declaration that moved past the quoted vocabulary is reported (`declarationDrift`) and never adopted silently; a version claimed in a file is reported as `declaredVersion` and is still not a publication.

alignment.rule: A difference between this package's quoted vocabulary and the declaration it consumes is reported as data (`declarationDrift`), registered in the frontend register, and never resolved by adopting a word this package cannot quote. With XA-19 resolved there is no tolerated difference left: the comparison requires exact agreement, and a future difference fails until a new open row is registered.
alignment.openQuestion: XA-11 remains open-for-manager: whether Skill ultimately belongs under the ai-foundation domain. Locking ai.skill@1.0.0 published the contract; it did not settle where Skill is modelled.
